task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: minutes / initiations / same-position minutes as predictors
methodological_questions: Does the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile gain most in the absent player's primary play types more often than chance and more often than the minutes, initiation-volume and same-position-minutes alternatives?
How should gain be defined (counts, rate per 100 possessions, share of own possessions) to avoid mechanical dependence on minutes and role?
Is the unit count adequate? The task records n=148 spells but only 11 cases.
How reliable are the derived play-type labels and initiator attribution?
How can regression to the mean and selection of the top gainer be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched role-player absence: paired dD_A +0.1151, n=96 matched pairs. [prior work] lists [prior work] and RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. It is a team-level identity measure, not a teammate-level gainer analysis.

Opponent three-point luck has split-half reliability of about 0.004, whereas other player-level measures reach roughly 0.43-0.59. Split-half reliability checks are therefore informative about whether a per-player measure carries signal. [prior work] lists RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY.
Player and teammate sequential play-type premiums were reported at small cell sizes (n about 30-70). [prior work] names [prior work] and [prior work], with the mechanism unclear.
A +3.3 ORtg adjusted effect for closeness to the engine mix was reported with no CI or test. The target shared outcome data. [prior work] lists RISK:BASE_RATE and RISK:LABEL_ERROR.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading specific play-type sequence or teammate premiums from small per-cell counts
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits are label/classification error and small sample; mechanism unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reporting an effect without CI or test, using a target that shares outcome data
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as no CI/test for +3.3, shared outcome data, and 3 of 6 cases being counter-examples.

evidence_establishes: Under [prior work][prior work], absences of connector-type players can be studied at the team level, with the recorded caveats of small samples and a mechanical floor.
Under [prior work][prior work], split-half reliability is an available check on whether a per-player measure carries signal.
Under FAM:[prior work] and [prior work][prior work], play-type labels and small cells are recorded as sources of error.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the teammate with the closest initiation profile is the largest gainer of the absent player's primary types.
Whether closest-profile similarity beats minutes, initiation volume or same-position minutes as a predictor.
own_inferences: No retrieved record tests this question, so prior work answers it at most indirectly.

Gain ranked in raw counts will largely favour high-minute or high-usage teammates, so the four predictors are collinear and the profile-similarity hypothesis is only informative if it adds beyond them.
Picking the top gainer from noisy per-teammate changes inflates winner's-curse and regression-to-the-mean effects, which also pushes the observed hit rate toward predictors correlated with volume.

With about 8-9 rotation teammates per spell, chance of picking the top gainer is roughly 11-13%. With n=148 spells the SE on a hit rate is about 0.027, so a hit rate of roughly 0.21 or more is detectable. With 11 cases only very large effects are detectable.
If initiation profiles are defined from the same play types used to define gain, similarity and outcome are partly circular.
uncertainties: It is unclear how 148 spells reduce to 11 cases. This may be an eligibility filter, such as a primary-type definition or a minimum-exposure threshold.
The definitions of 'primary types', the profile distance metric and the minimum spell length are not specified.
Lineup and coaching changes, injuries to others, and opponent and schedule effects during spells are not described.
Initiator attribution quality in the derived records is unknown; no validation is recorded for the derived play-type labels.
The 2025-26 data were complete at the as-of date, but whether any spells there are held out is unstated.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records are only tangentially related, but they reinforce the stated risks of small samples, label error and mechanical floors, pushing the decision from a straightforward proceed to proceed_with_changes. They add design requirements (a reliability check, CIs, and an explicit chance baseline) rather than any evidence on the hypothesis itself.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases are recorded as available. If this is the true analyzable count, the test cannot detect a moderate hit-rate advantage over the roughly 12% chance baseline. The test is only adequately powered if the 148-spell set is usable.
Top-gainer ranking by raw counts is mechanically tied to minutes and usage, so the alternative predictors are confounded with the outcome by construction.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tested whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer. [prior work][prior work] studied team-level identity displacement under connector absence, and FAM:[prior work] studied sequential play-type premiums; neither answers this question. The question is therefore treated as open.

risks.text: 11 cases versus 148 spells is ambiguous; detectable effects depend on which is used. Ties and small per-spell exposure also reduce power.
Minutes and initiations predict count gains mechanically, since more minutes means more opportunity to take over possessions.
Selecting the single largest gainer from noisy per-teammate changes selects on noise and regresses to the mean in later spells.
Per-teammate play-type rates over short spells and the profile similarity vector are noisy. Split-half reliability should be shown (see [prior work][prior work] for the precedent).
Derived play-type and initiator labels from play-by-play may be misclassified (FAM:[prior work] lists label/classification error).
Profile similarity and gain both come from the same derived play-type records; the same labelled possessions must not feed both.
Concurrent lineup changes, a teammate's own injury, opponent quality, the reason for absence and position-need all affect who gains.
The chance hit rate depends on the number of eligible teammates (roughly 1/8 to 1/9) and must be benchmarked per spell.
Four predictors and several definitions of gain and primary types create researcher degrees of freedom.
Roles and play-type mixes shift across 2022-26 seasons and within seasons, so the pre-absence profile window matters.

design.estimand: For each absence spell, the probability that the teammate ranked first by pre-absence initiation-profile similarity (distance between the teammate's and the absent player's play-type initiation distributions, Jensen-Shannon or cosine) is also the teammate with the largest gain, in rate terms, in the absent player's primary play types. This is compared with the chance hit rate of 1/k (k = eligible rotation teammates) and with the hit rates of three alternative predictors: most minutes, most initiations, most same-position minutes. The key contrast is similarity versus the alternatives, after conditioning on teammate volume.
design.unit: Absence spell: a team-game run in which a player of defined role is out while the team plays, defined by a minimum pre-absence exposure and a minimum number of absence games, excluding spells with other rotation absences where feasible.
design.sample: Absence spells from 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, from the 148 recorded spells, with the 11-case subset reported separately. Pre-registered eligibility: absent player with at least a fixed number of initiated possessions across at least a fixed number of games before the spell, a spell of at least a fixed number of games, and at least k eligible teammates. Teammates must have a minimum number of rotation minutes in both windows. The eligibility and exclusion counts will be reported.
design.power: Under chance hit rate of about 0.12 and n=148, SE is about 0.027, so a hit rate of about 0.21 or more is detectable at about 80% power (one-sided alpha=0.05). With n=11 only hit rates above about 0.35-0.40 are detectable, so the 11-case result is descriptive only. Report exact binomial or permutation CIs for each predictor and for the paired differences between predictors via McNemar-style or bootstrap contrasts over spells.
design.controls: Define gain as the change in the teammate's possession-share or per-100-possession rate in the absent player's primary types, versus the same teammate's with-player baseline, adjusted for the minute change. Derive the profile similarity from a pre-absence window disjoint from the one used to define primary types, or from a split of games. Use odd/even split-half reliability of the profile and of the gain. Add a multinomial or conditional-logit model of top-gainer with similarity, minutes, initiations and same-position minutes entered together, with team-season clustering, to test whether similarity adds beyond volume. Check the label by sampling and hand-audit of initiator attribution.
design.falsification: Permutation of teammate labels within spell to give the chance hit rate. Placebo: use pseudo-absences, i.e. games when the player played, with a random teammate set aside, to estimate the hit rate of similarity when no absorption is needed. Negative control: similarity computed from play types unrelated to the absent player's primary types. Also test whether similarity hit rate falls to chance when gain is defined on non-primary types. Reverse test: if the similarity predictor has no advantage over volume after conditioning, treat the hypothesis as rejected.
design.multiplicity: Primary test is a single pre-specified contrast (similarity versus the best of the three alternatives, with the primary metric of gain fixed in advance). The three alternatives and sensitivity analyses are secondary, with Holm correction across the four predictor-versus-chance tests. Exploratory definitions of gain, thresholds and primary-type counts are labelled exploratory and not used for the decision.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the similarity hit rate exceeds chance with a one-sided Holm-adjusted p<0.05 on at least n=100 eligible spells, and similarity significantly exceeds the best alternative or adds in the joint model after volume. Rejected if the upper 95% CI bound for similarity's advantage over chance is below 0.08, or similarity has no advantage over volume in the joint model. Otherwise inconclusive. Results from only the 11-case subset are not used for the decision.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-01. The 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21. Freeze the data snapshot and the eligibility code before any outcome is computed.
